sources.locator: PDF page 9, objective3.4 Power: generators and UPS; capacity planning.
UPS runtime definition and load-dependent runtime FAQs.
Runtime versus connected equipment; battery time while generators start. Only these claims used; no VA conversion formula taken from page.

questions.stem: A planned power-failure drill requires a critical service to stay running without interruption until generator power reaches the UPS input, with at least two minutes of battery runtime remaining at that point. The complete essential equipment load is 600 W; an optional display adds 400 W and can remain off without affecting the service. The UPS output limit is 1,500 W. Under the same test conditions, verified minimum battery runtimes are 12 minutes at 600 W and seven minutes at 1,000 W. After utility loss, the generator is ready in eight minutes and transfer to the UPS input takes two more minutes. Generator fuel/capacity, UPS compatibility and uninterrupted switching are verified for this drill; no other power source is available. Which plan satisfies the stated requirements?
options: Put only the essential 600 W on the UPS and keep the optional display off while the generator starts and transfers.
Put the essential equipment and display on the UPS because their combined 1,000 W is below its 1,500 W output limit.
Connect the essential equipment only to the generator, relying on its verified capacity once it starts and transfers.
Run the essential equipment on the UPS, shut it down at minute six, then restart it after generator transfer completes.
optionFeedback: Correct: protect only the essential 600 W. Generator power reaches the UPS input after 8 + 2 = 10 minutes; the measured 12-minute battery runtime leaves the required two-minute reserve. The optional 400 W load would reduce measured runtime to seven minutes.
Both loads fit the 1,500 W output limit, but their measured battery runtime is only seven minutes. Output watt capacity does not guarantee ten minutes of battery support or the required reserve.
The generator cannot supply the essential equipment during the first ten minutes. Without the UPS bridge, the equipment loses power at utility failure, violating uninterrupted operation.

A controlled shutdown may protect data, but it interrupts the essential service from minute six until restart. It does not meet the stated uninterrupted-operation requirement, even if restart succeeds.
questions.explanation: Correct: protect only the essential 600 W. Generator power reaches the UPS input after 8 + 2 = 10 minutes; the measured 12-minute battery runtime leaves the required two-minute reserve. The optional 400 W load would reduce measured runtime to seven minutes.
questions.taxonomyBlocker: No reviewed mastery identity for load-dependent UPS battery bridging; do not promote a power term or objective topic, or add an RTO/RPO role.
questions.familyRationale: Select a physical power bridge using load-dependent measured battery runtime and the time until usable generator input. Unlike restoration runbook summation or RTO naming, the power rating alone cannot decide adequacy and an optional load changes the supported duration. Different from m708 upstream network capacity and the manual-workaround throughput family.
questions.accuracyCheck: 600+400=1000<1500 W; required bridge=8+2=10 min; essential runtime12 minus bridge10=2 min meets stipulated reserve; all-load runtime7 minus bridge10=-3 min fails. No VA conversion, linear battery scaling, universal reserve or future reliability guarantee.
